faq.q: What’s the typical Marbella boat rental weather in April 2027?
faq.a: April in Marbella averages 19°C air temperature with 18°C sea temperature. You’ll get 8-9 hours of daylight, mostly sunny skies, and light westerly winds at 10-15 knots. Afternoon sea breezes can pick up, but conditions are generally calm and ideal for coastal cruising.

faq.q: Is Easter a busy time for boat rentals in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, Easter (4 April 2027) is peak season in Marbella. Puerto Banús fills up fast, so we recommend booking at least 2-3 weeks in advance. Our fleet of 15+ boats means you’ll find availability, but popular models like the Azimut 58 Flybridge or Mangusta 80 go quickly.

faq.q: What boat do you recommend for a family of 8 in April?
faq.a: For 8 guests, the Astondoa 40 (€749/2h) or Azimut 39 (€749/2h) are excellent value. Both are 12.5m and include a skipper, drinks, and snacks. If you want more space, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) offers flybridge seating and a cabin for cooler April afternoons.

faq.q: Do I need a jacket on a boat in Marbella in April?
faq.a: Yes, bring a light jacket or windbreaker. April mornings can be 15°C, and once the boat gets moving, wind chill drops the feels-like temperature by 3-5°C. By midday, it warms to 20°C, so layers are key. Our boats have shaded areas and cabins if you need a break from the breeze.

faq.q: Can I swim from the boat in April?
faq.a: Sea temperature is 18°C in April – swimmable but brisk. Most guests take a quick dip at Cala del Faro or Cabopino. We provide towels and fresh water showers. If you’re not keen, the sunset views from the boat are just as rewarding.

faq.q: What’s included in the charter price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden fees. For Tier B boats like the Mangusta 80, a jet ski is included free.

faq.q: Where do we depart from and what’s the best route?
faq.a: All boats depart from Puerto Banús. A popular 8h route heads east past Marbella Marina to Cabopino (30 min), then to Cala del Faro for swimming. Alternatively, go west to Estepona (45 min) for lunch at a chiringuito. Our skipper will tailor the route to your group.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book for April 2027?
faq.a: For Easter week (3-10 April), book by mid-March. For other weekends, 2 weeks ahead is safe. We accept WhatsApp bookings for last-minute spots. Contact us via the number on our site – we’ll confirm availability within 1 hour.

data.body_html:
Planning a Marbella boat rental weather April 2027 is all about timing and knowing what to expect. Easter falls on 4 April, and the Costa del Sol delivers mild 19°C air, 18°C sea, and calm seas perfect for a day afloat. Whether you’re after a 2-hour sunset cruise or an 8-hour exploration from Puerto Banús to Cabopino, this guide gives you real numbers, boat options from €749, and insider tips to make your charter seamless.

What’s the Weather Like in Marbella in April 2027?

April in Marbella is spring at its best. Average air temperature: 19°C (range 15-22°C). Sea temperature: 18°C – swimmable if you’re brave, but most guests prefer a quick dip followed by sunbathing. Wind: 10-15 knots from the west, with afternoon sea breezes that can reach 20 knots. Daylight: 8-9 hours (sunrise ~7:30, sunset ~20:30). Rain: only 4-5 days per month, so odds are in your favour.

Easter 2027: Book Your Charter Early

Easter week (3-10 April) is the busiest period for boat rentals in Marbella. Puerto Banús fills with yachts and visitors, and our fleet of 15+ boats sees high demand. To secure your preferred vessel – say the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) or the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) – book at least 2-3 weeks ahead. Last-minute spots are possible via WhatsApp, but don’t risk missing out.

Which Boat Should You Choose for April?

For groups up to 9, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, €749/2h → €2,299/8h) is a solid choice – covered flybridge keeps you dry if a shower passes. The Azimut 39 (same pricing) offers a similar layout. For 12 guests, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m) provides a spacious saloon and flybridge for cooler afternoons. If you want speed and style, the Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax) hits 40 knots – perfect for a quick hop to Estepona. All charters include a skipper, fuel, drinks, and snacks.

Best Routes for an April Day on the Water

From Puerto Banús, head east: 30 minutes to Cabopino (sand dunes, quiet coves), then 15 minutes to Cala del Faro for swimming (18°C water – bring a wetsuit if you’re keen). Alternatively, go west 45 minutes to Estepona – lunch at a chiringuito like La Escollera (fresh grilled fish). For a longer trip, continue to Sotogrande (1 hour) or Gibraltar (2 hours) – both offer unique views. Our skipper will adjust based on wind and your preferences.

What to Wear and Bring for April Boating

Layers are key. Start with a light jacket or windbreaker (15°C in the morning). By midday, you’ll be in a T-shirt. Sunscreen (SPF 50) is essential – the UV index reaches 6 in April. Sunglasses with a strap, a hat, and non-slip shoes (no black soles) are recommended. We provide towels, fresh water, and soft drinks, but feel free to bring your own snacks or a cooler. If you’re prone to seasickness, take a motion-sickness tablet an hour before departure – April seas are calm, but afternoon breezes can create a gentle swell.

Why April Is a Smart Time to Rent a Boat in Marbella

April offers the sweet spot: fewer crowds than July, lower prices (Tier A boats from €749/2h vs €1,000+ in peak summer), and pleasant weather. The sea is calm enough for families, and the scenery – snow-capped Sierra Blanca behind La Concha mountain – is stunning. Plus, you can anchor at Cala Cortés or Río Verde without fighting for space. It’s the perfect pre-summer escape.
